title: Energy–Flow Cosmology v1.2: Foundational Framework and Cross-Field Continuity
description: Presents Energy–Flow Cosmology (EFC), a covariant non-equilibrium thermodynamic field framework that extends General Relativity with a scalar energy-flow potential Ef, disformal matter coupling, and a Lyapunov-consistent dissipation structure. The theory reduces to GR in equilibrium, proposes a parsimonious parameter hierarchy with mild scale dependence, and outlines pre-registered Bayesian cross-prediction tests across rotation curves, weak lensing, SNe-Ia, and BAO. It also provides a functional bridge to variational free energy, enabling continuity to informational and biological systems, and introduces a unique observable: the Entropic Halo Temperature.

action.description: Conservative action: Einstein–Hilbert term plus an entropy-coupled scalar energy-flow field E_f with kinetic prefactor K(S) and potential V(E_f,S); matter couples via a disformal metric.

disformal_metric.description: Matter fields experience a disformal geometry controlled by the energy-flow field and entropy, sourcing effective dynamics without explicit DM/DE.

field_equation_covariant.latex: \nabla_\mu\big[ K(S)\, \nabla^\mu E_f \big] - \frac{\partial V}{\partial E_f} = J[E_f,S;\psi], \quad \frac{\partial V}{\partial E_f} = \lambda\, \sigma(E_f,S),\; \sigma \equiv \frac{\partial S}{\partial V}
field_equation_covariant.description: Scalar field equation linking the potential slope to an entropic driver σ; J encapsulates source terms induced by disformal coupling.

elliptic_core.description: Quasi-static, weak-field elliptic limit that generalizes Poisson’s equation and admits MOND-like p-Laplace regimes via K(S).

einstein_equation.description: Backreaction of the E_f field on spacetime curvature enters Einstein’s equations through its stress–energy tensor.

rayleigh_dissipation.description: Rayleigh dissipation functional introducing irreversibility; yields a finite-speed (Maxwell–Cattaneo) relaxation for E_f.

maxwell_cattaneo.description: Causal, time-asymmetric evolution equation ensuring a thermodynamic arrow and GENERIC/Onsager consistency.

effective_lambda.description: FLRW background with an emergent, time-dependent effective cosmological term from volume-averaged entropy production.

lyapunov_functional.description: Lyapunov functional demonstrating well-posedness and second-law consistency under the dissipative dynamics.

scaling_hierarchy.description: Minimal scale dependence and parsimonious parameterization shared across astrophysical datasets for true cross-prediction.

entropic_halo_temperature.description: Unique, directly testable EFC observable predicted from baryonic density without particle dark matter, comparable to X-ray/SZ profiles.

key_results.main_finding: Establishes a mathematically well-posed, Lyapunov-consistent, covariant non-equilibrium thermodynamic extension of GR with a single scalar energy-flow field, a parsimonious cross-scale parameter hierarchy, and explicit, pre-registered cross-dataset tests including a unique Entropic Halo Temperature signature.
datasets_used: Cluster/halo X-ray and SZ profiles (for Th)

sealed_predictions.statement: The Entropic Halo Temperature Th(r) derived from Eqs. (5), (13), and (14) matches X-ray/SZ temperature profiles when computed solely from baryonic density ρ(r), without invoking particle dark matter.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint X-ray and SZ profile measurements across a representative halo sample compared to Th(r) predicted from observed baryonic ρ(r).

sealed_predictions.statement: A single parameter vector Θ(μ), calibrated on SPARC rotation curves, will cross-predict CFHTLenS weak lensing, SNe-Ia, and BAO statistics without re-tuning.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Holdout Bayesian model comparison showing >3σ failure or decisively worse AIC/BIC/ln BF on CFHTLenS, SNe-Ia, or BAO using the SPARC-calibrated Θ(μ).

kill_criteria: KC1: Cross-prediction failure (NG-1) — The parameter vector Θ(μ) calibrated on SPARC rotation curves fails at >3σ on CFHTLenS weak lensing in true holdout testing without any re-tuning.

KC2: Thermodynamic halo test (NG-2) — The Entropic Halo Temperature Th(r) predicted from baryonic ρ(r) via Eqs. (5), (13), and (14) shows systematic disagreement with stacked X-ray/SZ temperature profiles across halos at fixed ρ(r).

KC3: Variational isomorphy break (NG-3) — The functional isomorphy to variational free energy is invalidated (e.g., required convexity fails), breaking the GENERIC/Onsager-consistent structure of the theory.
